title: A counted vector tail, and a packed compare mask driving a select, on A2 and A3
surface: muls and add with an explicit count= over a larger allocation; compare(predicate, x, y, CompareMode.GT) into a packed DT.uint8 mask tile; select(..., SelectMode.TENSOR_TENSOR, tmp_addr_buf=) with a DT.uint32 scratch address buffer; a dynamic GM shape symbol; kernel(mode="vec") from the a2 or a3 facade
study_for: `count=` is how a vector instruction is told its logical extent, which is not its allocation. The tile holds 128 lanes and 70 are live; the other 58 are allocated and transferred and never computed. 70 is chosen because it is neither a full tile nor a round fraction of one -- `check_domain` refuses a count that divides the capacity, since such a case could pass with the count ignored.

The predicate is *packed*: one bit per lane, so 64 lanes of comparison result live in a `DT.uint8[1, 32]` tile rather than in 64 bytes. That is the layout `compare` produces and `select` consumes, and reading it as one byte per lane is the mistake the shape makes visible.
`select` takes a scratch address buffer, `tmp_addr_buf`, which is a real allocation the caller owns rather than something the instruction finds for itself.

The answer for the select case is an element-wise maximum, and `check_domain` requires both sides to be chosen somewhere in the case. A mask read in the wrong direction is then wrong in about half the lanes instead of in none, and a select that always took one operand fails immediately.
The facade is an argument: `kernels(device)` decorates the same bodies with A2's or A3's `kernel`, so this source is both devices' example and `--device` runs it as each.
do_not_copy_when: You expect the lanes past `count=` to be defined. They are not written; here they are not even published, because the output is exactly the logical extent.
You are treating the predicate as one byte per lane. It is one bit per lane, and the tile shape says so.
You want `select` without a scratch address buffer. It needs one, and it is the caller's allocation.
Your device is not A2 or A3. The facade is checked; a different profile has its own vector vocabulary and its own mask layout rules.
